data.narrative:
Archer Aviation is a publicly listed operator in the Drones & Autonomous sector. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of four same-sector peers spanning similar valuation tiers, including Joby Aviation (public, $6.9B), Zipline (Series G, $7.6B), Nuro (Series G, $6.0B), and Elroy Air (Series B, $800M). No direct public comparables exist within the tighter valuation band, limiting the depth of peer triangulation.

The peer-median method was applied given the availability of recent valuation data across the four-company set. The median valuation across this cohort is $6.4B, with a range spanning $800M to $7.6B. This method implies an Archer valuation of $6.4B. The current market valuation of $3.33B sits 48% below the peer median, reflecting either a discount relative to the comparative set or divergence in growth trajectory and near-term revenue visibility relative to Joby and Zipline.

Triangulation across available methods yields a range of $5.5B (low) to $7.4B (high) with a median of $6.4B. Key uncertainties include the heterogeneity within the peer set—particularly the wide gap between Elroy Air at $800M and Zipline at $7.6B—and the stage mix (Series B through public), which limits direct comparability on capital efficiency and commercialization progress. Current market pricing suggests investor caution on Archer's path to revenue relative to nearer-term cash generation trajectories of peers.
